messages:
alex: Hey team - got a last-minute customer security questionnaire (SOC2/encryption/subprocessors/logs). Need quick canned answers we can paste back. Key asks: SOC2 status, encryption at rest/in-transit, customer-managed keys (KMS), list of subprocessors, and whether logs contain PII or need redaction. Can someone help draft?

rachel: I can draft. Quick facts: we are SOC 2 Type II (2024 audit) and we can provide the SOC2 report under NDA. For hosted API keys are provider-managed; Dedicated/Private support customer-managed KMS.

sam: For encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 for data at rest. For Hosted, disk and object storage encrypted with cloud KMS. Dedicated supports CMKs via customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) — note that on-prem Private can use HSM/KMS.

mike: On subprocessors: primary ones are cloud infra (AWS/GCP), monitoring (Datadog), Sentry for errors, Segment/Amplitude for analytics (only if enabled), and our hosting partners. We have a published list: https://redwood.ai/docs/security/subprocessors — can we point them to that?

alex: Good. Need a short answer about logs: do logs contain PII by default? We should be conservative.

julia: Default logs do NOT include raw user prompt text. We capture request metadata (model, latency, request_id, anonymized usage). We redact prompt/response content in hosted logs unless the customer opts into debug logging. We should include the regex/redaction example.

rachel: Here's a suggested paragraph we can paste into the questionnaire: "Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant (report available under NDA). All network traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Customers on Dedicated and Private deployments may configure customer-managed keys via supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK); Hosted uses provider-managed keys. We publish an up-to-date subprocessors list at https://redwood.ai/docs/security/subprocessors. By default, application logs do not contain raw prompt or response text; sensitive fields are redacted. We offer additional redaction and logging controls for customers with specific requirements."

sam: Add a small line about retention: "Logs and metrics retention varies by plan; we can provide retention windows on request and configure extended retention for enterprise customers."

mike: For the redaction snippet, propose this (we can paste technical detail if they ask):

```
# example redaction rule (server-side)
redact_rules = [
  {"field": "prompt", "pattern": ".{0,}?(cc|credit card|ssn|ssn:).{0,}?", "action": "replace_with_token"},
  {"field": "response", "pattern": "(?i)(ssn|social security|credit card|card number)", "action": "mask"}
]
```

julia: Also add: "Customers that require full control can deploy Redwood Private in their VPC or on-prem where no customer data leaves their network (subject to the deployment config)."

alex: This is great. Two quick asks: 1) Can someone confirm exact SOC2 date/period (quarter/year) to include? 2) Can we produce a short CSV of subprocessors for the support attach?

rachel: SOC2 Type II audit period: Jan 1, 2024 - Dec 31, 2024 (report issued Feb 2025). I'll confirm with compliance and update if needed.

mike: I can export the subprocessors CSV (INF-4271). Will attach to the ticket and link here.

security-bot: Ticket INF-4271 created by @mike for subprocessors CSV export. Status: open. :robot_face:

alex: Awesome — let's assemble final answers and send to customer by EOD. Rachel, can you produce a single paste-ready block that includes the SOC2 line, encryption lines, KMS note, subprocessors link, log redaction summary, and retention note? I'll review.

rachel: On it. Draft: "Redwood Security Summary:
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II (audit period: Jan 1, 2024–Dec 31, 2024). SOC2 report available under NDA.
- Encryption: All network traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Hosted uses provider-managed keys; Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or HSM.
- Subprocessors: Up-to-date list available at https://redwood.ai/docs/security/subprocessors. We can provide a CSV export upon request (ticket INF-4271).
- Logging and PII: By default, application logs do not include raw prompt/response content. Sensitive data are redacted server-side; customers can enable additional debug logging (opt-in).
- Retention: Log/metric retention windows vary by plan; extended retention is available for enterprise contracts."

sam: LGTM. :thumbsup:

julia: Minor nit: change "TLS 1.2+" to "TLS 1.2 or higher (TLS 1.3 preferred)".

rachel: Updated. Final draft posted to the ticket and copied into the questionnaire.

alex: Thank you everyone. I'll send the response and mark INF-4271 when we have the CSV. Closing loop: customer asked about subprocessors in EU — Mike, please ensure the CSV has region columns.

mike: Will do. ETA 2pm PT today.

alex: :raised_hands:
